title: Ireland's Budget Windfall Meets a Cost-of-Living Crisis That Numbers Alone… · 07 Sep
keywords: Ireland, Budget 2027, tax receipts, cost of living, inflation, energy prices, HICP, exchequer, fiscal policy, European Union, housing, public spending, Irish economy
notes: Ireland enters its 2027 budget cycle with unusually strong public finances, yet a persistent squeeze on household bills is testing the government's claim that the good times are being shared fairly. Tax receipts are running well ahead of last year, giving ministers rare fiscal room, but a near-10% rise in electricity prices and inflation still running at 3.4% are feeding public frustration. The gap between the headline figures and lived experience is fast becoming the defining political argument in Dublin.
